findings.description: The gate's `authoritative` mode now reads its selector from `.loa.config.yaml` (`implement_gate.mode`) and, once selected, trusts `tool_input.active_skill` as the skill-in-progress signal. The header comment itself concedes `tool_input` is model-authored and that no harness-set field exists. `.loa.config.yaml` sits at the project root, outside the `.claude/` System Zone fence, so the same agent the gate is meant to fence can first Write `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` and then self-attest `active_skill: implement` on every subsequent App-Zone Write/Edit. Authoritative mode is therefore strictly weaker than the heuristic default: it converts a fail-ask fence into a self-signed bypass.
findings.failure_mode: An agent (or an operator who enables the mode expecting stronger enforcement) gets a gate that any model-authored tool call can satisfy, silently removing the fail-ask on App-Zone writes outside /implement//bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the authoritative branch until the harness exposes a non-model-authored skill field, or AND it with the heuristic (.run RUNNING state) instead of replacing it. If kept, read the selector only from a System-Zone file and log a `compliance.mode.change` audit event when the mode differs from heuristic, so the opt-in is visible.

findings.description: The evidence recorder is triggered by model-authored input (`tool_input.active_skill` non-empty) and rewrites `.run/platform-features.json`. It runs before the Write/Edit `file_path` check, so any tool payload carrying the field fires it. It unconditionally sets `active_skill_available: false`, which clobbers whatever `detect-platform-features.sh` recorded, and if the existing file is not a single JSON object the `_ig_base` fallback is `{}` so the file is replaced wholesale with three keys. The `tail -n 1` on `select(type=="object")` also means a multi-document file silently picks the last object.
findings.failure_mode: A model-controlled payload can trigger a rewrite of a shared `.run/` state file, downgrading or discarding the platform detector's output; other consumers of `platform-features.json` read a file whose content depends on what the model put in a tool call.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the recorder after the Write/Edit `file_path` guard, write only the `active_skill_seen_at` and `active_skill_source` keys (do not touch `active_skill_available`), and skip the write when the existing file is not a single valid JSON object rather than replacing it.

findings.description: `rule_key` recognises a wildcard only when the body ends in `:*` or ` *`. A bare catch-all `Bash(*)` normalises to the exact key `=*` and matches nothing. In the allow direction this is merely conservative (reports missing), but in the deny direction a catch-all `Bash(*)` deny in any settings layer is not recognised, so the preflight reports every required Bash rule as allowed when Claude Code will in fact deny them. The deny-wins logic therefore has a blind spot for the broadest possible deny.
findings.failure_mode: Preflight passes while the runtime denies every Bash command, or an operator relying on the report to confirm a deny is in force gets a false 'allowed' answer.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a body of exactly `*` (after trim) as a universal wildcard key that covers every requirement for both allow and deny, and add a bats case for `Bash(*)` in each list.

findings.description: The new `anthropic:claude-headless` registry row declares `file_read/file_write/command_execution/network_access: false` and remote-model trust scopes, justified by the adapter running `claude -p --tools "" --permission-mode plan`. The notes admit an operator-set `extra.allowed_tools` in the catalog widens what the CLI can do, but nothing cross-checks the two: `test_current_generation_rows_mirror_the_4_7_scopes` deliberately excludes this row and no test asserts the catalog's `claude-headless.extra.allowed_tools` is empty. The headless hop is also the terminal fallback for `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-opus-5` and `claude-fable-5-1`, so an HTTP failure lands on it automatically.
findings.failure_mode: Capability declarations the permission model relies on (no file or command access) silently become false the moment `extra.allowed_tools` is set, with no test or load-time check flagging the drift.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a parity test that fails when `providers.anthropic.models.claude-headless.extra.allowed_tools` is non-empty while the registry row still declares all capabilities false, or have the headless adapter refuse `allowed_tools` unless the registry row is updated.
